versions.short: The bill would require mobile phone providers that offer satellite voice and data service to decide whether they will also send emergency alerts to their customers by satellite, and to notify the Federal Communications Commission of that choice. Providers that opt in would have to follow technical rules set by the Commission and could not charge an extra fee for satellite alerts. Customers who choose to opt out of receiving emergency alerts would be blocked from getting them by satellite. The Commission would have to propose rules within six months and issue a final rule within 18 months, in consultation with the Department of Homeland Security and the Federal Emergency Management Agency, with those rules designed to minimize the impact on other voice and data communications, including 9–1–1 communications. Providers that follow the law would be shielded from liability for satellite alert transmissions and for sharing subscriber information with public safety agencies.
